business_rules.name: Division by Zero Prevention
business_rules.description: When the selected operation is Divide, the divisor (num2) must not equal zero. If it does, the operation is rejected with an error message and execution is halted.
business_rules.action: Display error banner and halt script execution
business_rules.rationale: Division by zero is mathematically undefined; allowing it would raise a ZeroDivisionError and crash the application

business_rules.name: Floating-Point Precision Standard
business_rules.description: All numeric inputs and outputs are handled as floating-point numbers with up to 6 decimal places of precision, ensuring consistency across all four operations.
business_rules.action: format='%.6f' applied to both st.number_input widgets
business_rules.rationale: Ensures sub-integer values are correctly captured and displayed without silent truncation

business_rules.name: Default Operation is Addition
business_rules.description: When the application first loads, the operation selector defaults to 'Add' (index 0), providing a predictable starting state for users.
business_rules.rationale: Addition is the most common and safest default operation; it avoids accidental division-by-zero on first interaction

business_rules.name: Calculation Gated by Explicit Submission
business_rules.description: The arithmetic computation block executes only after the user explicitly clicks the 'Calculate' button. Changing inputs does not trigger a recalculation.
business_rules.rationale: Prevents partial or unintended calculations during input editing, improving UX reliability

business_rules.name: Exactly Four Operations Supported
business_rules.description: The application supports exactly four arithmetic operations: Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication, and Division. No other operations (e.g., modulo, exponentiation) are available.
business_rules.rationale: Keeps the application simple and focused on basic four-function arithmetic

business_rules.name: Result Displayed as Formatted Equation
business_rules.description: The computed result is always displayed as a human-readable equation in the format 'num1 SYMBOL num2 = result', making the calculation transparent to the user.
business_rules.condition: Successful computation (submitted == True AND no error)
business_rules.action: Render f-string equation in st.success banner
business_rules.rationale: Confirms the exact inputs used in the calculation, preventing confusion if inputs were misread

business_rules.name: Computation Details Available on Demand
business_rules.description: After a successful calculation, the raw computation data dictionary (operands, operation name, result) is available in a collapsible expander panel, but is hidden by default to keep the UI clean.
business_rules.rationale: Supports power users and debugging without cluttering the primary result view

decision_logic.name: Operation Routing
decision_logic.description: A four-branch conditional routes the submitted operation string to the corresponding arithmetic expression and assigns the appropriate display symbol.

branches.action: symbol = '÷'; guard check; result = num1 / num2
branches.outcome: Division result computed or error raised

decision_logic.default_branch: Divide (else clause) — relies on the selectbox constraining input to valid values only

decision_logic.name: Division-by-Zero Guard
decision_logic.description: Nested inside the Divide branch, this guard checks the divisor before the division is attempted. On failure it displays an error and halts execution.

branches.action: st.error('Division by zero is not allowed.'); st.stop()

decision_logic.name: Submission Gate
decision_logic.description: Guards the entire computation and display block; nothing executes unless the form has been explicitly submitted in the current re-run.

branches.outcome: Blank result area; form visible only

error_conditions.name: Division by Zero
error_conditions.user_visible_message: Division by zero is not allowed.
error_conditions.recovery_mechanism: st.stop() halts execution; user must correct num2 and resubmit
error_conditions.technical_detail: st.stop() raises a Streamlit StopException internally, preventing further script execution and avoiding a NameError caused by result being undefined
